response.reason: All three generic structures test a single metric (either final_third_entries or touches_in_penalty_area) in isolation, with no conditions and no opponent-profile rationale anchoring the cohort. The candidate is structurally distinct on two axes: (1) it tests two territorial metrics jointly under a single cohort contrast, requiring both to move together for the mechanism to hold; (2) the similar-opponent cohort is explicitly motivated by the upcoming opponent's HIGH home attacking territorial profile, meaning the cohort is not a generic similarity bucket but one conditioned on a specific opponent-profile axis. Neither of these structural features — joint dual-metric testing and opponent-profile-anchored cohort rationale — appears in any of the three generic structures. The self-critique correctly flags that opponent strength could partially explain the pattern, but the cross-window stability evidence (60.4 / 60.2 / 61.4) and the cross-referencing of Betis's home generation rate against Rayo's concession rate provide a falsifiable interaction that goes beyond a simple strength confound. The candidate is not overconditioned and the cohort does not collapse to the baseline.
